blindSummary:
This state/province is the only one in the country with a carried-out religious-law death-by-stoning sentence for same-sex acts in the modern record: on 28 June 2022 a religious-law court in a local government area of the state/province sentenced three men to death under a provision of the state/province's religious-law penal code of 2001, following arrest by the religious-morality police corps. Lower-level practice includes secret floggings (March 2014, four men, 15 lashes each) and a religious-law commission charging a dozen men over a "gay club" gathering (January 2014). LGBTQ+ groups warned the stoning could trigger similar cases across the country's religious-law states/provinces.

Mitigating institutional fact: the state/province's upper religious-law court has repeatedly quashed stoning sentences on appeal (two 2003 cases), according to an international human-rights organisation. However, the 2022 conviction and its public announcement by the religious-police head demonstrate active enforcement capacity. The unit's standing sits below the national baseline, reflecting the only actual capital-punishment-for-homosexuality event in the country plus ongoing religious-police arrests. It sits well below the state/province whose religious-police force is the most active, and far below another unit where religious-police activity is noted but no capital sentence has been imposed - both have comparable statutory text without a documented carried-out stoning.
